learning_outcomes.text: Apply fundamental concepts of magnetostatic and characterize magnetic field sources.
Apply fundamental concepts of time varying electromagnetic fields.

syllabus_topics: Electric field and Gauss's law (Coulomb's law, charge density, electrostatic equilibrium, movement in an electric uniform field)
Capacitors and dielectrics (electric displacement field, Displacement current)
Stationary currents and resistances (density of electric current, conductivity, Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's law, Joule's effect)
Magnetic field (magnetic force and flux density field, particle movement, Hall's effect)
Magnetic field source (force between wires with electrical currents, Ampere's law, magnetic flux)
Faraday's Law (electromotive force, Lenz's law, generators, Maxwell's equations)
Maxwell Equations, plane wave an optics

assessment_methods.method: Practical component (four laboratory experiences or individual project)
Written (two frequencies or global written test)

assessment_rules: The practical component has a 40% weight with a minimum grade of 9.5. The written component has a 60% weight and a 9.5 minimum grade, or 8 if the student attends more than 75% of classes.
bibliography: Physics and Science for Engineers with Modern Physics , Raymond A. Serway, John W. Jewett, 9th Edition, Thomson Learning.
Engineering Electromagnetics, Kenneth R. Demarest, Prentice-Hall.
Electromagnetics, Joseph A. Edminister, 2nd Edition, Schaum's Outlines Series - McGRAW-HILL.
